reason: Refuted as a stand-alone LB probe under the value lens: the realistic public gain is ~0, well below +0.002. The mechanism itself is verified and it transfers. x138 cell 0 sets REPAIR_DEADLINE_S=27000 counted from KERNEL_START_TS. In cell 5, _deadline_degrade switches off relink (with readmit nested inside it), gap close, gap2, safe divisions and linefit for every later dataset, and geffs are walked in sorted order. No learned component is involved, so there is no in-sample, 44b6-redundancy or node-multiplier risk. Public ~0: x138 with the guard scores 0.953, above our unguarded exp51 (0.950, same GPU phase per DIFF.md), and the guard was 'neutral alone on LB' (CONTEXT.md l.1431). A material degradation of public movies is therefore ruled out: 15% of all movies degraded on the public embryo would cost ~-0.028. The idea UNDERSTATES the per-movie loss. Safe divisions produce all forks (exp45 safe-div off: 0.947 -> 0.911 = 0.1 x divJ 0.36, RESULTS.md l.59), and divJ is micro-pooled (metrics.md l.142). Degrading a fraction g of a board's movies therefore costs ~0.036 g on divisions plus ~0.02-0.028 g on edges (lab: gap +0.013, linefit +0.0145, relink -0.0067, RESULTS.md l.104). That is ~0.05-0.065 g in total, not 0.025. Private value = P(fire) x g x ~0.055. P(fire on exp56) ~0.2-0.3 (guess): exp51 has the same GPU phase and finished inside a 7.5 h submit-to-score latency that includes queueing, and x138's tail differs by an unknown +-0.5 h. Expected private gain ~+0.002, and +0.008..+0.02 if it fires. The idea misses that whether it fires is observable for free: kernel runtime < submit-to-score latency. So latency(#34) < 7.5 h proves the guard never fired on exp56, the patch is worth exactly 0 there, and the same holds for #35/exp57b. Spending one of 21 slots on a guaranteed public tie is not justified.
fix_if_any: Use it as a zero-slot rider with a free gate instead of a probe. (1) Read the submit->score latency of #34 (exp56) and #35 (exp57b) tonight. If latency < 7.50 h, the guard provably did not fire on that file: drop the idea for it (gain exactly 0). (2) If latency >= 7.5 h, or for ANY heavier x138-family candidate (extra GPU pass, lowdet refine, second detector, DaughterNet insertion), build --patch deadline as proposed. Knob BIOHUB_REPAIR_BUDGET_S; 0 = byte-identical. Degrade only if elapsed + remaining x max(60 s, 1.3 x p90 repair_seconds) > 39,600 s, with a hard stop at 41,400 s. Better degradation order: drop relink/readmit/gap2 first and keep safe divisions + linefit (cheap and worth ~0.036 + 0.0145 per unit fraction) until the hard stop. Ship it only inside a probe that is submitted anyway for another reason. Validation: no-op dummy run sha256 == base CSV; a forced run (BUDGET_S=1) prints DEADLINE and writes a valid CSV. (3) In the finals, prefer the patched version of the F1 file if both scored and public is within 0.001. Do not use the public score to judge it.
realistic_public_gain: ~0 (expected <= +0.0003). A public degradation large enough to matter (>= 0.003) is ruled out by x138 0.953 >= unguarded exp51 0.950 and by the 'guard neutral on LB' history. LB noise 0.003 would swamp any residual.
realistic_private_gain: Expected ~+0.002 (guess: P(fire) 0.25 x P(tail not public) 0.8 x E[g | fire] 0.2 x 0.055). Conditional on firing: +0.008..+0.02. Exactly 0 if latency(#34/#35) < 7.5 h. Never negative once the patched run has scored validly: public and private come from the same run.
